rationale_overall: This week's pool produced no US-listed, liquid, pure-play ticker with a genuine buildup-phase catalyst clearly stronger than the four managed holdings. Filtered noise: government/agency items with no listed equity (ISRO village mapping, IAF drone-swarm RFP, DRDO warship testing, Kudankulam AERB clearance, Iran nuclear rhetoric, Canada fighter-jet observer talks, Singapore Home Team satellite plan); private/pre-IPO companies (SpaceX Falcon 9 launch and the speculative SpaceX IPO framing, India's Vikram-1 private rocket); foreign OTC/thinly-traded juniors that fail the liquidity floor (Cauldron Energy on ASX, F4 Uranium Corp financing, Kraken Robotics on TSX Venture); academic/competition human-interest filler (robotics competitions, university AI centres/deans); a stale republished 2022-dated defense article; and generic listicle/commentary pieces ("Top Quantum Computing Stocks," "AI Chip Rally Pushed SMH Higher," CBRE AI build-out commentary) that name no new actionable ticker. The Nvidia quantum-computing and unified-AI-model stories, plus the Nvidia physical-AI/Asian-partners rally, reinforce the existing NVDA thesis rather than surface a new name. Cadence's raised AI-chip-design guidance is a real US-listed catalyst but reads as an already-appreciated adjacent play, not a clearly stronger rising-wave vehicle than current holdings, so it does not clear the bar for a swap this week. Ontario's Darlington SMR milestone reinforces the nuclear-buildup thesis already expressed via SMR rather than motivating a new add. No fundamental thesis breach surfaced for GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, or SMR. Holding the watchlist unchanged this period.
